chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Writing "A Lover Is Blue" and "Traveling Light"
summary: He started composing; Mundy arranged "Traveling Light" and claimed the tune, and Johnny Mercer wrote lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I never did too much arranging myself. I composed, but I never did too much arranging. But I -- I was more of a composer then than arranger. I wrote -- I started writing tunes I guess way back because some of the tunes that I had written I never do anything with them until later. But when I went with Earl Hines, one of the tunes that I had written, Charlie Carpenter wrote the -- I don't know if you knew Charlie.

He wrote the lyrics for -- and Charlies was band boy with Earl Hines back there in those days. He and another little guy named Dunlop and I wrote -- the first thing I wrote was "A Lover is Blue". And Tommy Dorsey recorded it. And that's when Jack Leonard sang with Tommy Dorsey. And Tommy recorded it. And the next thing I wrote was "Traveling Light", and almost lost that tune because I went up to Jimmy Mundy, and he said he was going to make an arrangement on it, you know.

And I went up to his house. He lived in New York then. And I was with Earl Hines. And I showed him I went. And he -- I didn't even know he made an arrangement on it. He was writing for Whiteman back there then. And he made an arrangement on it. And the story I got was somebody asked him

whose tune was that, and he said it was his tune.

So then, Johnny Mercer wrote lyrics for it. And the record came out and my name wasn't on it. So, I got so angry about it because all the guys knew it was my tune, but I didn't have sense enough to copyright it. So, you know, but I knew I could prove it was my tune. But that's finally when my name got on the tune. So, I had to blame Munday for not telling them it was my tune.

I didn't mind if he had cut himself in on it, said it was he and mine. But to leave me completely out of, I felt -- I felt hurt about it. And I never did really kind of get over that but I don't hold it against him because of the fact that we were friends. You just don't do that to a friend of yours, you know. This is -- Budd Johnson knows the whole story because Budd was with Earl back then at that time.
